issues.legal_issue: Criminal liability for alleged dishonest retention of property cannot be established beyond reasonable doubt where the accused’s title or agency status depends on unresolved civil disputes over ownership of the property.
material_facts: The accused was convicted under Section 409 of the Indian Penal Code for allegedly retaining land and its profits that he was said to hold as trustee and agent for the complainant.
The accused claimed that he had bought the land for charitable use, while the complainant claimed that he held it for her as a benamidar.

The nature of the accused’s relationship to the property was difficult to determine from the evidence, and the property had been transferred to a trust that would be a necessary party to a civil title dispute.
The complainant still had an available civil remedy to establish her rights to the property and seek its return.
issues.conclusion: The Court dismissed the appeal against the acquittal, holding that criminal liability could not be fastened beyond reasonable doubt before the complainant’s rights and title to the property were properly established in a civil suit.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the requirement that criminal liability be established beyond reasonable doubt. Although the charge was under Section 409 of the Indian Penal Code, the Court did not decide whether criminal breach of trust can be committed in respect of immovable property, nor did it set out the elements of that offence. It held on the circumstances before it that the essentially civil dispute over title had to be resolved before criminal liability could be satisfactorily adjudicated. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: appeal_against_acquittal and criminal_charge_depends_on_disputed_property_ownership and ownership_evidence_inconclusive and civil_title_remedy_available

predicates.appeal_against_acquittal: The prosecution appealed a judgment acquitting a person who had previously been convicted.
predicates.criminal_charge_depends_on_disputed_prop: The criminal accusation alleged that a person dishonestly retained or dealt with property said to belong to another, and depended on the accused’s alleged role or obligation concerning that property.
predicates.ownership_evidence_inconclusive: The evidence did not establish whether the accused held the disputed property for another or owned it in the accused’s own right.
predicates.civil_title_remedy_available: The person claiming the property could pursue a civil proceeding to establish title and seek its return.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an acquittal in a criminal case dependent on disputed property ownership, the evidence leaves ownership unresolved, and a civil title remedy is available, the appeal is dismissed and the acquittal is upheld.
